title: Deposition of inscribed tablets in the Sacred Spring at Aquae Sulis
summary: Across the Roman period, inscribed lead or pewter tablets were rolled or folded and deposited in the Sacred Spring at Aquae Sulis. The surviving corpus includes roughly 130 personal/private prayers, many connected to perceived injustice. This EVENT records the material deposition practice without treating the modern label 'curse' as a complete account of every participant's motive.

time.note: Range follows the Roman Baths institutional collection description.

historicity.note: Physical tablets and archaeological context strongly support the deposition practice.

uncertainty: Individual tablets differ in wording, date, and motive.
The modern category 'curse tablet' can obscure prayers for restitution or justice.
alternative_interpretations: Private prayer for restitution or justice.
A broader ritual petition whose intent depends on the individual inscription.

review.note: Canonical scope is the material/epigraphic deposition practice, not a single reconstructed motive.
